_metadata.rubric: x01 expansion rubric (owner style examples, clicks-when-explained bar, explanation checked), 2026-10-18
_metadata.independence: I read only x01-c-review-input.json and no other file, repository content or web source; the only other file touched is this output, parsed afterwards to check it is valid JSON.

hints.reason: Moon via the Apollo lunar program, Eagle via Apollo 11's lunar module and the famous 'The Eagle has landed'; the explanation is accurate.

best_available.why: A clean historical double hit with a quotable payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair; nothing to change.

hints.reason: Agent via a secret agent going undercover; mole via the playful 'under cover' underground pun, and the spy sense of mole backs it up.

best_available.why: Works on both the spy sense and the burrowing-animal pun.

pairs.pair_note: The explanation could also say that 'mole' is spy slang for an undercover agent, but it is accurate and charming as written.

hints.reason: Both sides via Aesop's fable 'The Fox and the Grapes'; the fox is the best-known Aesop animal, and the grapes come in through that one fable.
Grape via the idiom 'sour grapes'; fox via the fable that gave us the idiom, a satisfying click once explained.

best_available.why: Points squarely at the fable that holds both words, whereas SOUR leans toward the grape side.

pairs.pair_note: Both are good. SOUR is more fun but leans on the grape side; AESOP is the more even, fairer clue.

hints.reason: Painting via the Sistine Chapel ceiling, turtle via the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle named Michelangelo; both facts are correct.
Painting via Leonardo da Vinci and the Mona Lisa, turtle via the Ninja Turtles' leader; both facts are correct.

best_available.why: Leonardo is the more purely 'painter' name (Michelangelo is equally a sculptor), and he is the turtles' leader.

pairs.pair_note: These are the same idea twice; serve one. DONATELLO would be weaker because he was a sculptor.

hints.reason: Crab via Cancer and scorpion via Scorpio; the explanation is accurate.
Both have pincer claws, crabs on their front legs and scorpions on their pedipalps; a direct physical-feature link.

best_available.why: A neat categorical link that feels a little cleverer than a shared body part.

pairs.pair_note: Both are solid. Watch the board: ZODIAC collides with RAM, BULL, GOAT, LION or FISH, and PINCERS with LOBSTER.

hints.reason: Santa via Santa Claus; claw via the homophone 'claws'; a simple pun that clicks instantly.

best_available.why: The natural pun linking these two words.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: CLAUS sounds exactly like the plural of the target CLAW, but it is a different word with its own meaning, not a spelling of the plural, so I treat it as an allowed pun rather than synonym_of_target. It gives CLAW away by sound, which makes it easy rather than unfair.

hints.reason: Milk via its well-known calcium content, bone via the calcium stored in the skeleton (about 99% of the body's); the explanation is accurate.

best_available.why: The textbook link, familiar from 'milk builds strong bones'.

pairs.pair_note: Straightforward and fair.

hints.reason: Pupil via a school as a place of learning, fish via a school of fish; a classic double meaning.

best_available.why: A crisp double meaning that hits both words fully.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. PUPIL also carries an eye meaning, which adds a nice bit of misdirection.

hints.reason: Chick via the peep sound and the chick-shaped candy, Easter via Peeps as an iconic U.S. Easter-basket treat.

best_available.why: A brand that is literally a chick sold at Easter, which is very satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Strongly American, which matches the intended audience.

hints.reason: Doe via Bambi's mother, rabbit via Thumper; both facts are correct for the Disney film.

best_available.why: A beloved story that contains both words.

pairs.pair_note: Watch the board: BAMBI also points at DEER, SKUNK or OWL if any of them is present.

hints.reason: Donkey via the Nintendo character Donkey Kong, king via King Kong; both are giant apes, so the explanation holds.

best_available.why: Two famous compounds finished by one word, a real 'oh, nice' moment.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: Goat via 'Three Billy Goats Gruff', troll via the same tale's troll (the 'gruff troll' line is a bonus); naming the story calls up both characters.
Troll via the classic troll under the bridge, goat via the goats crossing it in 'Three Billy Goats Gruff'.

best_available.why: Only one story uses this word, and that story holds both targets.

pairs.pair_note: GRUFF is the more distinctive clue; BRIDGE is fine but leans on the troll side.

hints.reason: Both are well-known flightless birds; the explanation is accurate.

best_available.why: A direct, fair categorical link; KIWI read as a fruit adds mild misdirection.

pairs.pair_note: Watch the board for OSTRICH, EMU, DODO or CHICKEN.

hints.reason: Penguin via its tuxedo-like black-and-white coloring, waiter via the formal black-tie uniform; a familiar visual metaphor that the explanation keeps as one.

best_available.why: A familiar image that ties a bird to a job with a smile.

pairs.pair_note: Good. The explanation correctly frames the penguin side as 'looking dressed for dinner' rather than as a literal fact.

hints.reason: Ship via its crew, skeleton via the idiom 'skeleton crew'; the explanation defines the idiom correctly.

best_available.why: An idiom twist that makes SKELETON click nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. A skeleton crew of pirate ghosts makes it even more vivid.

hints.reason: Piano via practicing musical scales, reptile via scaly skin; a classic double meaning.

best_available.why: A clean double meaning, with a witty explanation.

pairs.pair_note: Watch the board for FISH, DRAGON or JUSTICE.

hints.reason: Amazon via its Echo smart speaker, bat via echolocation; both facts are correct.

best_available.why: The brand twist on AMAZON (players may think of the rainforest first) makes a satisfying reveal.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: Snow via Snow White (and white snow), dwarf via both the Seven Dwarfs and the white dwarf star; a double route on each side.

best_available.why: Snow White plus white dwarf is a lovely layered link.

pairs.pair_note: WHITE is a broad color word, but the Snow White story locks it to this pair.

hints.reason: Both via the compounds sandstorm and snowstorm; the explanation is accurate.

best_available.why: Two everyday compounds; fair and quick.

pairs.pair_note: Fine but low on surprise. Watch the board for THUNDER, BRAIN, RAIN or FIRE. Alternatives such as CASTLE (sandcastle, snow castle) or MAN (sandman, snowman) are worth considering; SNOWMAN plus SANDMAN might delight more.

hints.reason: Weather via the compound 'weather vane', rooster via the classic rooster figure on top of a vane; the explanation is accurate, and the rooster side clicks once you picture it.

best_available.why: The iconic rooster weather vane ties the two together.

pairs.pair_note: The weather side is immediate; the rooster side is a familiar image rather than a word link, but it is fair. A note for a second opinion: some players may read VANE as 'vain' (the proud rooster), which is a happy accident.

hints.reason: Boxing via the boxing ring, Saturn via its rings; the explanation is accurate.

best_available.why: A crisp double meaning that reaches across sport and space.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: Flower via bees collecting nectar, honey via bees making it; the explanation is accurate.

best_available.why: The perfect natural clue, in the spirit of GOLD + PIRATE -> TREASURE.

pairs.pair_note: Obvious, but correctly so.

hints.reason: Flower via the flower bud, taste via taste buds; a clean double meaning.

best_available.why: A neat double meaning with a small 'aha'.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; it pairs nicely with the FLOWER + HONEY pair as a contrast.

hints.reason: Both via the idiom 'extend an olive branch', a peace offering; the explanation is accurate.
Peace via the dove as a peace symbol, olive via the dove carrying an olive branch in that symbol (and in the Noah story).

best_available.why: The idiom 'olive branch' covers both words in one familiar phrase.

pairs.pair_note: Both are good. DOVE leans on the peace side, and BRANCH is the more balanced clue.

hints.reason: Planet via Venus, plant via the Venus flytrap; both facts are correct.

best_available.why: A memorable name shared by a planet and a famous carnivorous plant.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the near-identical spelling of PLANET and PLANT adds to the fun.

hints.reason: Bear via Smokey Bear, forest via his long-running 'Only you can prevent forest fires' campaign.

best_available.why: An iconic U.S. mascot who is literally both words.

pairs.pair_note: The slogan was updated to 'wildfires' in 2001, but 'forest fires' remains the famous phrase, and the explanation says 'decades', which is fair.

hints.reason: Paper via origami as paper folding, crane via the paper crane as origami's signature model.

best_available.why: Pins the bird sense of CRANE, which could otherwise be read as the machine.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: Closet via clothes hangers, cliff via the compound 'cliffhanger'; a satisfying compound-plus-object twist.

best_available.why: A real 'oh, nice' moment once 'cliffhanger' lands.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: Both via the compounds Ice Age and Stone Age; the explanation is accurate (the Ice Age movies add familiarity).

best_available.why: Two famous eras finished by the same word.

pairs.pair_note: Watch the board for BRONZE, IRON, GOLDEN or SPACE.

hints.reason: Titanic via the iceberg it struck, salad via iceberg lettuce; both facts are correct, and the 'sinks into your salad' line is playful rather than false.

best_available.why: An unexpected but airtight pairing of history and lunch.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Volcano via volcanic eruptions, soda via a shaken soda fizzing over (and the classic baking-soda volcano); the idea is sound, but the explanation mentions only the soda side.
hints.fix: Rewrite the explanation to name both sides, e.g. 'Volcanoes erupt, and so does a shaken soda, or the baking-soda volcano from the school science fair.'

best_available.why: A natural link; the science-fair volcano adds a second route.

pairs.pair_note: Only the explanation needs a touch-up.

hints.reason: Computer via data measured in bytes, cookie via the homophone 'bite'; a light pun, and the cookie side is a little thinner.
Computer via the computer chip, cookie via the chocolate chip; a clean double meaning, with a funny explanation.

best_available.why: A true double meaning on both sides, with no pun needed.

pairs.pair_note: CHIP is clearly stronger. BYTE is acceptable as a pun but leans on spelling, and 'bite' fits almost any food.

hints.reason: Ice cream via the sundae dessert, Sunday via the identical sound; the explanation is accurate.

best_available.why: The perfect homophone bridge between these two words.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: SUNDAE is a homophone of the target SUNDAY and a type of ice cream dish, but it is neither a synonym nor a spelling of either target, so I pass it. It is easy, but it delights.

hints.reason: Alps via the Swiss Alps, cheese via Swiss cheese; both are familiar phrases.

best_available.why: Two common compounds that share one adjective.

pairs.pair_note: Fine. 'Swiss cheese' is a U.S. name for Emmental-style cheese, which does come from Switzerland, so the explanation holds. Watch the board for WATCH, ARMY, KNIFE, BANK or CHOCOLATE.

hints.reason: Bird via birdsong chirps, cricket via the chirp crickets make by rubbing their wings; both facts in the explanation are correct.

best_available.why: A shared sound, plus a nice fact about how crickets make it.

pairs.pair_note: Solid. The sport meaning of CRICKET is British-leaning but irrelevant here, since the insect sense is universal in the U.S.
